personality_one_liner: A forensic, highly-structured investigative utility that uses stark contrasts, hard borders, and raw data exposure to empower victims with clear, factual evidence.

spacing.rule: Use rigid grids, edge-to-edge sections, hard alignment, and exposed spacing systems. Avoid soft padding; use structured visual tension.

dont's: Never use glassmorphism or blur in Brutalist personality. Rely on solid surfaceSecondary blocks and thick borders.

screens.name: Dashboard
screens.purpose: Central command point to launch the 5 scan engines and view system readiness.

states.error: Stark red block 'SYSTEM OFFLINE' with retry.

screens.layout: Top hero section featuring a stark, high-contrast abstract data image. Below, a rigid 2-column grid of bordered cards for 'Text Analysis', 'Photo Scan', 'Profile Check', 'Phone Lookup', and a full-width block for 'Comprehensive Full Scan'. Use thick 2pt borders for structure.

screens.name: Text Scan
screens.purpose: Input chat and profile text to receive a LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH risk verdict.
screens.layout: Single-column form. Monospaced labels above rigid multiline text areas (surfaceSecondary bg, hard border). No horizontal scrolling. A sticky 'ANALYZE TEXT' stark black button locked to the bottom safe area.

screens.name: Photo Scan
screens.purpose: Manual checklist of 7 visual manipulation flags to generate a photo risk verdict.
screens.layout: List of switch rows with thick dividers between them for the 7 flags (missing shadow, glasses issue, etc.). A segmented control for Observation Quality (Good/Partial/Poor) with sharp corners. Sticky 'GENERATE VERDICT' button at bottom.

screens.name: Profile Analysis
screens.purpose: Numeric inputs and bio text to evaluate profile concern level.
screens.layout: Single-column input. Use native numeric keyboards for followers, following, posts, photos, account age. Label above input. Monospaced fields. 'Contacted First' toggle block. Sticky primary CTA.

screens.name: Results View
screens.purpose: Forensic, evidence-based report of the risk level returned by any scan.
screens.layout: Top-to-bottom flow. Massive hero summary block with solid color (success/warning/error) mapping to LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH risk. Beneath it, compact evidence cards detailing fired categories and exact metrics. Heavy use of monospaced typography for 'Artifacts' and 'Traces'.

screens.name: History
screens.purpose: Local scan history list to track past investigations.

states.empty: Magnifying glass illustration + 'NO PREVIOUS SCANS RECORDED'.

screens.layout: Vertical list of scans. Each row has a thick left-border indicating risk color (green/yellow/red), monospaced timestamp, scan type, and thick bottom divider. Tap opens Results View.

hero_background.alt: Abstract blue data network lines and dots

empty_history.alt: Magnifying glass sits near a laptop on a table

instructions_to_main_agent: Implement Brutalist styling strictly: use 0 border radius everywhere (including buttons and cards). Use `borderStrong` (2pt thick) for focused inputs, structural cards, and primary buttons.
Do NOT use glassmorphism, blurs, or shadows. Depth is created purely through thick borders and stark color contrasts.
Form design must follow a single-column layout with monospaced labels placed ABOVE the inputs. Use `surfaceSecondary` for text area backgrounds to distinguish them from the white canvas.

Ensure 'Sticky CTAs' (e.g., ANALYZE TEXT, GENERATE VERDICT) are anchored at the bottom of the screen above the home indicator, allowing scrollable content to pass behind them (though in brutalism, a solid background block behind the button is preferred over blur).
Result screen risk blocks must be edge-to-edge, heavily saturated (e.g., neon green for safe, warning yellow for medium, signal red for high), with high-contrast text.

If rendering text on the `hero_background` image, apply a solid top-to-bottom gradient scrim to guarantee legibility, or encapsulate the image within a hard-bordered square and place text outside of it.
Use Phosphor icons in a consistent filled or regular weight across the app. Do not mix weights.
Wire up haptics per the `haptics` block in this JSON. High-risk verdicts should specifically trigger `notificationError`.
